questions.text: An unordered list contains n distinct elements. The number of comparisons to find an element in this list that is neither maximum nor minimum is
questions.solution:
Take any 3 elements and compare them (3 comparisons). The middle one of the three is neither the overall maximum nor the overall minimum.

This is a constant number of comparisons.

Answer: [latex]\Theta(1)[/latex]

questions.text: The minimum number of JK flip-flops required to construct a synchronous counter with the count sequence (0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3,0,0,...) is __________ .
questions.solution:
The sequence 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3 has 8 steps before repeating. Equal outputs at different steps must still be different internal states, so 8 states are needed.

[latex]2^3=8[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 flip-flops

Answer: 3

questions.text: Assume that for a certain processor, a read request takes 50 nanoseconds on a cache miss and 5 nanoseconds on a cache hit. Suppose while running a program, it was observed that 80% of the processor's read requests result in a cache hit. The average read access time in nanoseconds is __________.
questions.solution:
Average = 0.8 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 + 0.2 [latex]\times[/latex] 50 = 4 + 10 = 14 ns

Answer: 14

questions.text: A computer system implements a 40-bit virtual address, page size of 8 kilobytes, and a 128-entry translation look-aside buffer (TLB) organized into 32 sets each having four ways. Assume that the TLB tag does not store any process id. The minimum length of the TLB tag in bits is _________.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Page offset: 8 KB = [latex]2^{13}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 13 bits, so page number = 40 [latex]-[/latex] 13 = 27 bits
- 32 sets [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 index bits

Tag = 27 [latex]-[/latex] 5 = 22 bits

Answer: 22

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
I. The complement of every Turing decidable language is Turing decidable
II. There exists some language which is in NP but is not Turing decidable
III. If L is a language in NP, L is Turing decidable

Which of the above statements is/are true?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: decidable languages are closed under complement [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II: every NP language is decided by a (time-bounded) Turing machine [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- III: same reason [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True

Answer: Only I and III
